title: team-guardrails-scenarios-and-wires
content:
Purpose:
Purpose: sketch and capture interaction flows for a "team guardrails" area in Org > Settings that helps admins define, simulate, and rollout access constraints for teams and service identities. This doc is intentionally exploratory — focuses on scenario-driven UX, a dry-run simulator (policy impact preview), and audit integrations that help reduce misconfigurations during canary rollouts.

Context and problem:
- We get frequent support requests where a new service account or API key either has too many permissions or breaks a downstream job. Admins need tools to: visualize impact, test changes without applying them, enforce post-deployment checks, and quickly revert.
- Current Console exposes role creation and key management but lacks: a) proactive simulation, b) team-level guardrails (scoped defaults + overrides), c) lightweight audit replay for investigating incidents.

Goals (what success looks like):
1) Admins can define team-wide guardrails (deny lists, approved actions, mandatory MFA for key creation) in under 5 minutes.
2) Before applying changes, admins can run a dry-run simulation that reports which services/jobs would break (top 10 likely impacted) and suggests minimal permission deltas.
3) Console shows an augmented audit-log view with replay + snapshots so SRE/cust-success can fast-track root-cause.
4) UX integrates with existing rollouts (canary / A/B policy) so new role templates can be rolled out safely.

Primary personas:
- Org Admin (security/compliance): needs guardrails, policy enforcement, audit evidence.
- Platform Engineer / SRE: needs simulation and quick rollback; cares about service account lifecycle.
- Developer (power user): needs a clear path to request exceptions and see why access is blocked.

High-level feature concepts and wireframes (text sketches):
1) Team Guardrails landing (left nav: Org > Team guardrails)
   - Top summary strip: team selector (dropdown), active guardrail profile name, last evaluation timestamp, 'simulate' CTA, 'apply changes' (disabled until simulation green).
   - Tiles: "Active constraints" (deny list, allowed resources, required key rotation / MFA), "Recent Violations" (live count), "Open Exceptions" (requests).

2) Guardrail Policy Editor (two-column canvas)
   - Left: policy blocks (Allow/Require/Deny) with quick presets (e.g., "No wildcard storage write", "No raw-data export"). Each block shows: scope (teams/services), conditions, expiration.
   - Right: impact preview panel (graph + text) that updates live as you edit. Shows: affected service accounts, potential broken jobs, sample API calls blocked.
   - Inline control: 'simulate at time' (now | last 24h | last 7d) to let admins run against historical telemetry.

3) Role Template + Policy Diff modal
   - When creating/updating role templates you get a side-by-side diff: current template vs proposed. Buttons: "simulate", "save draft", "publish to team".
   - Small checkbox: "Require reviewer approval" (ties into rollout hooks).

4) Dry-run Simulator flow (core UX element)
   - Inputs: target team(s), timeframe for snapshot (last N days), traffic sample ratio (10%|100%), optional whitelisted services to ignore.
   - Output: table with columns: entity (service account / job), impact (block/alert/no change), example request, suggested minimum rule change. Top row shows a risk score (0-100) and estimated work to remediate (low/med/high).
   - Export button produces a PDF/CSV for change review and compliance evidence.

5) API Keys & Service Account lifecycle panel (integrated)
   - Key creation flow includes guardrail enforcement step: "This team requires rotate-every-90d" + show existing keys + last rotated by. Forbidden actions show inline justification.
   - Service account creation wizard includes a "scope-by-template" picker and simulated impact preview right in the wizard.

6) Audit Log augmented view (investigation-first)
   - Primary columns: timestamp, actor, action, target, outcome, policy-trigger (if applicable).
   - Context pane: when you click a row, show 'Related simulation snapshots' and 'Policy history at that time' so you can see what guardrails were in effect.
   - 'Replay' control: rerun that actor/action pair against a sandbox environment (sampled) to reproduce failure (requires dedicated infra flag).

Interaction notes and edge cases:
- Simulation accuracy: we will label results with confidence bands (low/medium/high) and show why (missing telemetry, rare code paths).
- Time-traveling simulations should be read-only; changes must be applied against current policy.
- Exceptions: support a short-lived exception token that bypasses guardrails for a labeled reason + approver. Exceptions show up in audit log with TTL and revocation action.
- Multi-team overlap: if a service account belongs to multiple teams, show aggregated policy and highlight the most restrictive constraint.

Backlog grooming (candidate tickets / priorities):
P0: Simulation engine integration (backend) + basic UI for one-team snapshot (JIRA-4601).
P0: Guardrails policy schema + presets (no-wildcard-storage, block-open-egress) (JIRA-4599).
P1: Role template diff modal + publish workflow + approval hook (JIRA-4610).
P1: Audit log context panel (link to snapshots) (JIRA-4623).
P2: Replay sandbox and 'replay' button (infra gating) (JIRA-4635).
P2: Exceptions tokens w/ approver flow and TTL (JIRA-4640).
P3: Support historical sample ratio and export (csv/pdf) (JIRA-4652).

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Admin can create a team guardrail with at least 3 presets and save as a profile.
- Admin can run a dry-run simulation over last 24h and see at least 5 example impacted entities when applicable.
- Audit log rows include a 'policy-trigger' column when guardrails blocked or allowed an action.
- Role template update requires a simulation run before publish (soft enforcement).

Open questions / risks: 
- Data retention and cost: storing snapshots for arbitrary past windows could be expensive. We should start with 7-day retention and sample-based replays.
- Signal availability: some internal jobs don't log full request/actor metadata — simulation will underreport. Need instrumentation plan.
- Governance: which teams can author guardrails vs who can only request exceptions? Default is Org Admin only, but team admins need some claim.
- Legal/compliance: exported simulation PDFs might be requested by auditors — ensure they redacts PII.

Design notes (micro-ux):
- Use compact rows for tables (dense view) with inline pills for policies.
- Color coding: green = allowed, amber = warning (would be affected), red = blocked. Hover reveals reason.
- Inline help: short contextual tooltips; link to 'what is a guardrail' Confluence doc.

Next steps / action items (owners):
- Marco Li: draft API endpoints and sample payload for simulation (due 2024-10-20).
- Sofia Martinez: initial wireframes (mobile/responsive considerations) + Figma link (due 2024-10-18).
- Daniel Kim: SRE feasibility check on replay infra + cost estimate (due 2024-10-25).
- Evelyn Park (me): consolidate this doc with Confluence page and create initial JIRA epic.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally high-level: want feedback on what 'simulation' should assume and the minimum viable signals we need from telemetry.
- Prefer conservative initial scope: one-team simulation, 7-day window, exportable results.

Raw brainstorming fragments (working):
- "policy impact map" idea: small matrix showing which services touch resources; could be useful for on-call.
- "fast-fail publish": if simulation shows high-risk, block publish and require two approvers.
- Shortcuts for developers: Request exception -> autosummarized justification + pre-filled approver list.

References / inspiration:
- Cloud IAM policy simulator (GCP) UX patterns.
- Internal incident postmortems where config change caused downstream failures (see JIRA-3012).

End.
